To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the extracted strands from highly compacted Nb{sub 2}Al cable showed some degradation of J{sub c}.
the J{sub c}, n and the current limit due to flux jump of Nb{sub 2}Al strands are almost the same as the extracted ones from a highly compacted Rutherford cable.
the Nb{sub3}Al strands in the Rutherford cable show a relatively low J{sub c}-degradation, but large flux jump in low field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of high field accelerator magnet technology using high current density Nb{sub 2.5}Ti and Nb{sub 5}Al conductors.
the fabrication and the properties of Nb{sub 2}Al strands and Rutherford cables.
the characteristics of Nb{sub 2}Al/Cu Rutherford cable.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Nb{sub 2}Al/Cu is a promising candidate for future high field superconducting magnet technology.
